Inbox by Gmail

Google’s experimental email client, launched in 2014 as one of the first full Material Design apps: a blue app bar, white cards, and a red action button.

Source
Official Gmail Blog: “An inbox that works for you” (22 October 2014)
Creator
Google
Made
2014 (announced 22 October 2014; shut down 2 April 2019)
Style
Material Design (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Bright, orderly, friendly
Evidence
Opened the two images in Google’s announcement post on 28 September 2026: inbox-nexus6-500.png (500 × 884, the app on a Nexus 6) and bigtopblog_fullres.gif (1000 × 592, a close-up of a Purchases bundle). Not stored.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Sundar Pichai announced Inbox on the Official Gmail Blog on 22 October 2014 as “a completely different type of inbox”. Gmail Blog.

Wikipedia: Inbox was announced on an invitation-only basis on 22 October 2014, released to the public on 28 May 2015, and shut down on 2 April 2019. Wikipedia: Inbox by Gmail.

Observed

  • A bright blue app bar holds a hamburger menu, the white title “Inbox”, a pin toggle, and a search glyph. The status bar above it is a darker blue.
  • Messages sit in white rows on a pale gray ground, with gray section labels “Today” and “Yesterday”. A Purchases bundle is a white card with a soft shadow and square corners, holding flat gray inner tiles with product photos.
  • Bundle labels are colored words: brown “Purchases”, cyan “Promos”, each with a count on a light tint of the same color.
  • A round red action button with a white plus floats over the lower right corner of the list with a soft shadow.

Why it belongs

Inbox uses the accent rule in its textbook form: a blue primary and a red action button, with category colors used only for small labels.

Borrow

Give each content category one hue and use it only for its label and a light tint behind the count.
